description: type: Video Browsing; caption: #Wilderness Construction: Luke begins renovating the interior of the stone house, plus free wild chestnuts to gather until your hands are tired! #Outdoor Construction #Stress Relief; ocr: Wild stone village house. Even if the corner is difficult to operate, Ike watches dramas.; asr: This is truly an enviable life. To escape the hustle and bustle of the city, a man returns to his hometown and inherits his ancestors' dilapidated old house. Over two and a half years, he personally transforms it into an exquisite dream home, not only handcrafting various pieces of furniture but also enjoying oversized grilled meat skewers at every meal, elevating outdoor living to new heights. As the weather has been getting hotter recently, grapes have reached their harvest season, though unfortunately they don't belong to Luke's family, so he'd better stick to renovating honestly. The fireplace in the corner is too old, and its heating effect couldn't be much good anyway. Luke tears it down cleanly in no time, along with the mottled, peeling walls that are heartbreaking to look at - clearing them all away is the best solution. At this moment, light rain begins to fall outside. Running on the roof, the waterproofing is very well done, allowing him to focus on working inside. The original house had two fireplaces to better heat the rooms on both sides. Since Luke has already removed the one on the other side, there's no reason to keep this one either. In the afternoon, he brings over his father's mixer. After connecting it to the diesel generator, he needs to apply some grease to the gears to make the mixer work properly and produce smoother mortar, which he evenly spreads on the walls. This is still to fill in small gaps and also to reinforce the walls and improve the stability of the stone wall's overall structure. During the drying time, he can't sit idle for a moment. He digs a row of deep holes behind the house to plant newly purchased saplings. In another ten years or so, this place will present an entirely different scene. The next morning, considering the jungle's humid climate, Luke brings over a roll of asphalt felt, planning to waterproof the ground. He presses the edges inward to create creases, making the material fit more closely to the walls. Then he uses intense flames to burn the edges, and while they show signs of melting, he presses them against the stone foundation on the wall, bonding them together forever. Even at corners where it's difficult to operate, Luke switches to a smaller spray gun to handle every detail properly. The joints between two pieces of asphalt felt must also be bonded using the same method, giving moisture no chance to enter the interior. Still not satisfied after doing all this, he applies strong waterproofing at the joints before contentedly enjoying the afternoon sunlight with his dog. After a brief rest, he prepares to harden the ground. First, he adds polypropylene fibers to the water, which greatly improves the concrete's tensile strength. Then he fixes lightweight rebar on the ground to adjust the overall level. After confirming there are no problems, he can bring in the concrete for comprehensive pouring throughout the interior. With the rebar on both sides as reference, he can mindlessly push and pull the scraper back and forth until the surface becomes flat and smooth. When the ground is completely dry the next day, Luke remembers the wall damaged when removing the fireplace. He takes this opportunity to install a ventilation opening, so that in the future, just by lighting the fireplace on one side, warmth will spread to the adjacent room, truly wasting no heat at all. The weather in October becomes cool, and chestnuts ripen at this time of year. They can be easily shelled with a foot stomp. Following the principle of never holding back when something is free, Luke picks a full five and a half pounds, making a cut in each chestnut so they'll open more easily when roasted. After just half an hour of waiting, the soft, sweet chestnuts are ready. He sends the dog off to play first, then Luke savors them carefully. After eating his fill, his strength is greatly restored. He can easily lift wooden boards weighing over ten pounds to seal under the eaves, preventing wild friends from making their homes there. After securing them with bolts, he evenly applies mortar into the gaps, ensuring that not even an ant can enter. The old beams, after years of weathering, have long since oxidized and blackened on the surface. Luke carefully grinds them with a grinding machine to restore their former glory. The door frame area cannot be overlooked either - everything must undergo a teeth-grinding sanding process before continuing to shine for the cottage. Suddenly, strong winds blow outside, cruelly toppling roadside trees, but Luke's cottage remains as steady as a rock, allowing him to focus on working indoors. description:
type: Video Browsing; caption: 【Xiaopang Animation】Folk Tale: The Coffin Bearer--Episode 01 #SandSculptureAnimation #PopularityIncentivePlan #FolkTale; ocr: Folk tale. Coffin Bearer. Episode 01. Old video reupload. "Coffin Bearer" original author: Guan Laojiu. Happy Hui. Wanting to save one's life, to be continued. Next episode uploading.; asr: My name is Xiao Pang. My grandfather was a famous corpse bearer in the surrounding villages. Later, my father, who was a Red Guard, threw him and all his tools into West Mountain Gully. He forbade touching those supernatural things. Grandma cried at home every day. I hated my father and wanted to go to West Mountain Gully to bring Grandpa back, but Grandma stopped me. However, on the seventh day after Grandpa was taken away, something happened in the village. That night, the village chief came to our door in a panic with several villagers. As soon as the village chief entered the courtyard, he asked with a frightened expression, "Xiao Pang, how much of your grandfather's skills have you learned?" I hesitated for a moment and asked, "What happened?" The village chief sighed and said, "Old Guizi at the village entrance has died. If we don't bury him properly, there will definitely be big trouble."

Hearing the village chief say this, my expression changed too. Old Guizi was a very special person in the village. He was full of strength. When village children misbehaved, their mothers would use Old Guizi to scare them. Grandpa had also told me before that it would have been good if Old Guizi had moved away while alive, but if he died here, the entire village would likely suffer. Thinking of Grandpa still in West Mountain Gully, my expression changed. If we couldn't bury Old Guizi today, given the strength in his body, he would surely transform after death. Looking at Grandma, who was equally panicked, I knew I couldn't leave. Grandpa hadn't come home yet. So I turned to the village chief and said, "Wait for me. I'll get some tools. Don't let too many people know, or there'll be trouble." The old village chief nodded excitedly. I went back to my room, picked up a hoe, and dug out a bundle from the corner in a few strikes. This was what Grandpa had hidden before he left. My father hadn't found it, and now it had become my only hope.

When I came out with the bundle, I noticed the moon in the sky was giving off an eerie aura. As soon as I arrived at Old Guizi's house, my heart sank. Old Guizi's room was eerily emitting black qi. Seeing this, I quickly said to the village chief, "The situation is bad. There's too much yin energy in Old Guizi's house. I'm afraid by midnight he'll transform into a corpse." The village chief's face turned pale and he said trembling, "Those men went to Carpenter Liu's to get a coffin. They'll bring it over soon, and we'll bury him tonight." I nodded and said, "Then let's split up. I'll prepare Old Guizi first, and you go find a few strong men." The village chief was startled, having forgotten about the corpse bearers, and then turned and ran off.

Watching the village chief's retreating figure, I took out a yellow talisman from the bundle and stuck it on my shoulder. At the same time, I grabbed a handful of glutinous rice in my hand and walked into Old Guizi's room. As soon as I entered, I suddenly felt gusts of cold wind blowing at me. Just then, I saw Old Guizi in the corner, his eyes staring fixedly at the half-broken cleaver stuck in his neck. I was so scared that I broke out in a cold sweat. This Old Guizi had actually transformed. Old Guizi lay in a pool of blood, the smell of blood drilling into my nose, making me nauseous. But I still steeled myself and grabbed Old Guizi's hands, slowly dragging him out of the room.

Looking at Old Guizi's corpse, I breathed a sigh of relief. Earlier I was afraid Old Guizi had died of illness, leaving a complete corpse. Now that he had cut his own neck and most of his vital blood had drained away, it would be very difficult for him to transform into a corpse. Moreover, we would bury him soon, so there shouldn't be any major problems. After dragging him out, I reached out and pulled the cleaver from his neck. I took out binding rope from the bundle and, after much effort, tied Old Guizi up tightly. Still not reassured after doing this, I took out glutinous rice from the bag and sprinkled several handfuls on Old Guizi's body.

Just as I was breathing a sigh of relief, I heard someone shouting outside the courtyard, "Xiao Pang! Xiao Pang! The corpse bearers and coffin are here!" I turned to look and indeed the courtyard was full of people. Four strong men were carrying a coffin, with the village chief and several villagers standing beside them. I raised my head and shouted to them, "Bring the coffin in." Hearing this, the corpse bearers' faces immediately changed, and they said with trembling voices, "That's not good. It's so dark inside. I think we should go to West Mountain Gully and invite Old Master back. Xiao Pang is too yo

What he never expected was that he would encounter his former senior brother and first love at the sect. Watching the two of them like a celestial couple, the young man's heart was filled with mixed feelings. name: How do braces straighten teeth? #BracesCorrection #ScienceExplainer
description: type: Video Browsing; caption: How do braces straighten teeth? #BracesCorrection #ScienceExplainer; ocr: Braces correction. The real power lies in what happens before the correction. This is the entire process of braces correction: you think they're pulling your teeth, but actually they're gently bending your bones. And what leverages all of this is the shape-memory metal wire in the brackets. At the beginning, the doctor applies adhesive to the tooth surface and attaches brackets to each tooth as anchor points. The position and angle are precisely calculated, and finally the metal wire is threaded through and secured with rubber bands. The braces are then fully installed. At this point, the metal wire on the braces begins to exert force. It's made of nickel-titanium alloy, called an archwire. Its characteristic is that no matter how you bend it, as soon as it comes into contact with human body temperature, it will slowly return to its initial arc, and the teeth will be gradually pulled toward the ideal position. Interestingly, as far back as ancient Egypt, people already had tooth correction technology. Archaeologists have discovered metal wires wound between teeth on mummies, equivalent to a primitive version of archwires plus brackets. However, lacking modern mechanical design, they relied entirely on physical pulling force to adjust the bite.; asr: The key to all this is the shape-memory metal wire in the brackets. Initially, the doctor applies adhesive to the tooth surface, then attaches brackets to each tooth. The position and angle of each bracket are precisely calculated. Finally, the metal wire is threaded through and secured with rubber bands, completing the braces installation. At this point, the metal wire on the braces begins to work. It is made of nickel-titanium alloy, called NiTi wire. Its characteristic is that no matter how you bend it, once it comes into contact with body temperature, it gradually returns to its original arc shape, and the teeth are pulled bit by bit toward the ideal position. Interestingly, as far back as ancient Egypt, people already had teeth straightening techniques. description: type: Video Browsing; caption: Smoother than oil? The real power of liquid nitrogen cold fitting! #BroKnowledgeEncyclopedia #ContentInspirationSharingProgram #PopularityIncentiveProgram; ocr: Liquid nitrogen shrink fitting, old-timer's tale. After soaking in liquid nitrogen, the parts won't fit in anymore.; asr: The old master dipped the steel sleeve into liquid nitrogen, then inserted it into the engine—it went in smoother than if it had been greased. Yet in some places, when installing tight-fitting parts, people either slather on grease like crazy or pound away with a sledgehammer. Many assume this must mean the parts were machined too small, but the truth is exactly the opposite. This is the mechanical industry's most hardcore black technology: liquid nitrogen cold assembly. When metal parts are thrown into liquid nitrogen at minus 196 degrees Celsius, the temperature plummets instantly, the distance between atoms contracts tighter, and the dimensions directly shrink by dozens to over a hundred micrometers. Just like these balloons freshly pulled from liquid nitrogen—still wrinkled together—they slowly puff back up at room temperature. Metal works on the same principle. While it's still contracted, you must immediately install it. After returning to room temperature, it regains its original size, and the entire structure is essentially naturally locked in place, even more solid than hydraulic press fitting. But liquid nitrogen isn't omnipotent. Extremely low temperatures make materials extremely brittle. Look at this sponge—normally you can knead and squeeze it however you want, but after soaking in liquid nitrogen, a light tap shatters it completely. So liquid nitrogen cold assembly has three iron rules: no hammering, no bumping, and absolutely no dragging, because metal warms back up too quickly. Workers only have a window of about ten seconds to complete the assembly. When you see them operating at lightning speed, they're not rushing—they're racing against the warming. Once the time limit is exceeded, the part can never be inserted again.; actions: type: watch, play_duration: 77, played_loop_cnt: 0, is_complete_play: True, is_fast_forward_play: True, is_backward_play: True, is_enlarge_play: False

description: type: Video Browsing; caption: When Sun Wukong was trapped under the Five Elements Mountain by Buddha, did Patriarch Bodhi take action #QuickTalkDrama #JourneyToTheWest #QuickGrowthPlan #FilmAndScreenFutureStar @KuaishouFilmAndTVCreators(O40300198) @KuaishouHotTopics(O40300129); ocr: Sun Wukong was pinned under the Five Elements Mountain by the Tathagata Buddha. Whether Patriarch Bodhi came to his aid or not, the Victorious Fighting Buddha was ultimately not killed but instead was granted the title of Victorious Fighting Buddha. This is a dramatization of "Journey to the West," purely for entertainment purposes and unrelated to reality. After Sun Wukong was pinned under the Five Elements Mountain, the Dragon King of the Jing River appeared. He was well-versed in the teachings of Confucianism, Buddhism, and Taoism, could only achieve immortality, and his longevity equal to heaven was maintained by ginseng fruit. He was a deity of the highest rank.; asr: After Sun Wukong was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain, did Patriarch Bodhi intervene or not? Why was Sun Wukong, who had committed heinous crimes, ultimately not killed but instead granted the title of Victorious Fighting Buddha? Even stranger, throughout all of Sun Wukong's troubles, not a single fellow disciple came to his aid. It should be noted that when Sun Wukong first met Patriarch Bodhi, the patriarch personally stated he had disciples across 12 generations, with Wukong being the tenth generation's youngest disciple. This means Sun Wukong had at least nine senior brothers, and their abilities were considerable. After Sun Wukong was pressed under Five Elements Mountain by Buddha Tathagata, these nine senior brothers never appeared, and even Patriarch Bodhi didn't speak up. Were they truly afraid of Heaven's power and hiding, or was this all deliberately arranged by Patriarch Bodhi? The answer to this question is far more complex than what we see. Just after Sun Wukong was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain, a very mysterious figure appeared in Chang'an City. This person was named Yuan Shoucheng. No one knew how, but his divinations were never wrong. Fishermen in the city followed his advice and always returned with full catches. However, over time, the fish in the water were nearly depleted. Upon learning this, the Jing River Dragon King was furious. He transformed into a scholar, found Yuan Shoucheng, and challenged him to predict when it would rain the next day and how much. After quickly performing a divination, Yuan Shoucheng said it would cloud over at chen hour, thunder at si hour, rain at wu hour, and stop at wei hour, with a total of 3 feet 3 inches and 48 drops of water. The Jing River Dragon King listened with disdain, believing Yuan Shoucheng was just a charlatan, because when it would rain was entirely up to the Jade Emperor - no second person could possibly know. If there were news, he as a dragon king would certainly be the first to know. So he made a harsh wager: if Yuan Shoucheng was right, he'd give him 50 taels of gold; if wrong, he'd smash Yuan's sign and drive him out of Chang'an. Afterward, he returned to the Dragon Palace to tell others about this. But then something strange happened - the Jade Emperor sent someone with an imperial decree ordering the Jing River Dragon King to make rain over Chang'an the next day. Most terrifying was that the time, location, and amount of rainfall matched Yuan Shoucheng's prediction exactly. Upon receiving the order, the Jing River Dragon King was scared unconscious. When he awoke, he realized Yuan Shoucheng was no ordinary person. But to win against Yuan Shoucheng, he still followed his advisor's suggestion and arbitrarily changed the rainfall amount and timing. After the rain, he went to Chang'an, smashed Yuan Shoucheng's stall, and tried to drive him out of the city. "Others may not recognize me, but I recognize you. Hmph, you're that Jing River Dragon King. What? You altered the Jade Emperor's decree by three inches and eight drops of rain. Don't you know this violates heavenly law? What did you say? Hmph, you'll inevitably face the executioner's blade at the Dragon-Beheading Platform." Hearing this, the Jing River Dragon King was terrified out of his wits and immediately knelt, begging Yuan Shoucheng to show him a way to survive. Little did he know, this was exactly what Yuan Shoucheng wanted. But he was still one step away from his ultimate goal. So he told the Jing River Dragon King: "I certainly cannot save you, but I can point you to a way out. Tomorrow at the third quarter of wu hour, you will be beheaded by the human official Wei Zheng. This Wei Zheng is a minister of the Tang King. If you can beg the Tang King to detain Wei Zheng on the execution day and prevent him from going to the Dragon-Beheading Platform, you might have a slim chance of survival."
